crops.observation: Actually inspected the 576x2016 native label sheet at original resolution (192px panels). Reference has red only along the upper-left edge, a top sliver and lower-left corner; nearly all methods invent a red central three-lobed island from the converted RGB while losing part of the true upper-left patch. Q12 removes that true patch but preserves the false central island. Q06 and Q11 suppress both, with tiny spurious residuals; Q08 hollows the false island without restoring the missed reference. Q15 is explicitly pixel-blocked. Q04/Q05 retain N08-like shapes; Q13/Q14 remain near C17. Support variants agree. These changes do not establish native architectural recovery.

Actually inspected all23 outputs in the native 256px crop at original resolution. The H&E crop is almost entirely gray glass with sparse debris, reference/coarse zero. B23/P11 label it uniformly green, Q02/Q03 almost uniformly green with small holes. Q01 removes most of the blanket but leaves discrete green speckles and small rings, while all common-support candidates including repaired Q12 keep it white. This confirms Q01's useful gray-background sensitivity and residual debris failure. It is an unscored foreground diagnostic, not proof of higher segmentation accuracy.

Actually inspected the native 256px epithelial-edge crop and all23 masks at original resolution. Common-support algorithms preserve the upper-left glass, with a thin green rim between it and the red epithelial band. B23/Q03 fill glass green, P11 leaves only a small wedge, Q01 nearly fills it, and Q02 preserves a larger but still undersized wedge. Q06 stipples and partly destroys the thin red lining; Q12 thins/straightens its left end and loses fine contour. Q11 slightly changes thickness. Q13/Q14 remain close to C17; Q15 is unmistakably blocky. Reference marks the empty glass green, so its overlap cannot certify physical foreground accuracy.

Actually inspected all23 outputs in the 768x2592 native label sheet at original resolution (256px panels). The repaired Q12 now preserves the parent gray evidence along the thin supported cleft border: the v1 false red lowest-ID fringe is absent in this current crop. Its white-gap silhouette now follows the common-support family. However, that common gap covers only a portion of the physically empty H&E cleft; substantial glass is still gray-labeled. P11/B23/Q01/Q03 fill essentially the entire crop gray and Q02 leaves only a tiny white fragment. Reference/coarse are zero throughout this crop, so it diagnoses support/implementation behavior and cannot validate class accuracy. Other appearance and palette children preserve the common-support gap; no fine class distinction appears here.

Actually inspected the native 256px crop at original resolution across all23 outputs. H&E is almost empty glass with a thin detached fragment at upper-right and main tissue along right edge. Reference/coarse blue polygons cover much more empty space. B23 makes an angular blanket, P11/Q01 broaden the main edge, Q02 joins the detached fragment to it, and Q03 adds square blocks. Common-support masks including repaired Q12 retain the separated fragment and more physical glass. Q01 also leaves tiny exterior blue speckles. Most appearance variants are almost identical because only blue is plausible locally; Q15 blockiness appears on the support boundary. This is strong evidence of reference/physical-support mismatch, not evidence that higher IoU foreground is better.

Actually inspected all23 current native panels. Reference is a green neck between red areas, with no cyan. J01/M04/B23/P11/Q01/Q02/Q03/Q07/Q08/Q09/Q10/Q11 put broad false cyan inside that green neck. N08/Q04/Q05 remove most cyan but retain a small cyan spot at the lower bulb; Q05 therefore does not completely avoid this error at native scale. C17/B22/Q13/Q14 avoid cyan and follow a simpler green neck. Q06 avoids broad cyan but adds edge stipple; Q12 avoids cyan yet changes neck geometry. Q15 remains visibly blocky. These are spurious class assignments from RGB-likelihood modeling, not verified novel tissue regions.

Actually inspected all23 masks in the native 256px top-left crop at original resolution. This crop contains stained tissue throughout and does not show the separate exterior glass wedge. Reference is mostly red with a thin upper green band; all outputs overassign green on upper/right and left contours. Q06 has stippled edges, Q11 changes the lobes, Q12 pools away most small green detail, and Q15 has square steps. N08/Q04/Q05 give slightly different lobes and a small green central spot; Q13/Q14 stay near C17. Native-support variants agree locally. These observations cannot establish native behavior in the lower-left exterior glass.

Actually inspected the full native 256px crop and all23 outputs at original resolution. Reference has three distinct red small islands, but coarse labels and converted RGB are uniformly green here; every method outputs solid green and fully misses all three. H&E contains visible cells and tissue variation, yet the fixed RGB supplied no local red evidence. Neither Q12 connectivity, Q15 agglomeration nor any transported appearance model recovers those regions. This is direct native evidence of a shared small-region failure; color-outlier hypotheses are diagnostics, not semantic class recovery.

scope: Eight actual native label-sheet inspections at original display resolution. Targeted development repair check; not independent validation. No overlay inspection claimed.
conclusion: PUMA11 Q12 false red fringe is absent after repair. Other22 native masks remain exactly equal to v1 by the separate parity report. Gray-glass filling, lost thin structures and absent-coarse classes remain unresolved.
